column1: # day-cp-steps.tsv — P1324. The ClarityPledge sub-day's half of /day's step manifest.
# The dispatcher discovers this file at run time — `$ROOT/scripts/day-<name>-steps.tsv`,
# alongside the same glob that finds the sub-day itself — and registers it with
# `day-step.sh add-manifest`. It is never hardcoded in the dispatcher (CLAUDE.md Dynamic
# Discovery), and this file never names a home-directory path, so `day-cp.md`'s contract
# ("do not read or write dispatcher state") holds: the sub-day is handed the runner's path
# in $DAY_STEP, exactly as it is already handed $SINCE and $DUE_VERDICT.
# Columns and the meaning of kind/policy: see ~/.claude/scripts/day-steps.tsv, which owns the format.
# Short version: cmd = must run through `day-step.sh run` so the exit code is recorded;
# attest = an MCP or Skill call with no exit code, recorded with a sentence of evidence;
# hard = cannot be skipped; skippable = genuinely conditional, recorded with a reason.
# WHY THESE IDS AND NOT FINER ONES. One id per WAVE, because a wave is already one bash call
# in day-cp.md — so the ledger entry and the thing that executes are the same unit, and no
# prose rewrite is needed to make the receipt honest. Finer ids would need the waves split,
# which this spec explicitly deferred (P1324 Alternatives Considered).
# Measured coverage of these ten across the 13 real passes since 2026-08-28, from transcript
# tool-calls: Wave 1 and the Supabase half of Wave 2 ran 13/13; Sentry 10/13; Mixpanel 7/13;
# the privilege-floor check inside Wave 3 8/13. Everything here has been silently dropped at
# least once except Wave 1.
